fatal_errors: The proposed nitrogen interstitial intervention does not reconstruct the targeted Ti-induced fcc/C14 dual-phase alloy or its rapid-quench stabilization.
The cited evidence concerns strain and L10 Pt ordering in FeCoNiMnCu-based films; it provides no direct observation that dilute nitrogen produces tetragonal FeCoNi or increases its coercivity.
A 20% increase over undoped FeCoNi is not sufficient to establish coercivity greater than the prior FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives without quantitative measurements of those baselines.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses coercivity through a single, testable symmetry-lowering intervention and uses a reasonable undoped FeCoNi control. Its experiment has an explicit coercivity threshold and structural measurements, although annealed nitrogen-free controls and a nitrogen-dose series would better separate nitrogen effects from processing-induced strain or microstructural changes. Scientifically, the proposal is only indirectly supported: the cited work validates the general connection between reduced symmetry, anisotropy, and domain-wall pinning, but not the key nitrogen-to-tetragonality step. The claim that distortion enhances spin-orbit coupling is also imprecise; distortion can convert existing spin-orbit coupling into greater anisotropy without necessarily strengthening the coupling itself. Relative to the hidden result, it misses Ti addition, fcc/C14 coexistence, chemical segregation, antiferromagnetic Ti-sublattice coupling, measurements through 400 K, multiple magnetic transitions, and the approximately 667 Oe coercivity outcome.
